labels.label: def:capstar

the honest energy ∫⁻ |∇v|²_g ∈ [0,∞] (energy), so cap* ∈ [0,∞] with inf ∅ = ∞ and infinite-energy functions contribute ∞, not the junk 0 of dirichlet
Bochner integrals: 0 on non-integrable functions; under MeanPoincare and TraceBound every u ∈ D has integrable values and traces
capWeight_nonneg; sum_capWeight once S ≠ 0

hypotheses.note: ell_smul, ell_add (on integrable functions), ell_one (V ≠ 0, S ≠ 0, finite measures), ell_bounded (under TraceBound and L² values); l.161 is context of the definition, outside its span l.163–173

questions: θ = a_N cap*/(c_N S) is real in the paper; here θ uses cap*.toReal, which is 0 if cap* = ∞ (excluded by lem_capstar under its hypotheses). Reading taken: θ is only used where 0 < cap* < ∞.

labels.label: lem:capstar

hypotheses.note: IsFiniteMeasure (vol g), IsFiniteMeasure (bvol g j)
through the Poincaré inequality MeanPoincare: ∃ K, ∀ v, val v ∈ L² ∧ ‖v − v̄‖²_{L²} ≤ K‖∇v‖² (the proof's « by Poincaré », l.394; K = λ_1⁻¹). Discharge on a manifold reading: T-perf-poincare

∃ j, bvol g j ≠ 0 (S > 0) and the trace theorem TraceBound, which is YamabeScaffold.Trace's TraceIneq with w12Sq unfolded (Iff.rfl, checked in a scratch file importing both); its manifold discharge is Mfd.Reads.traceIneq (scaffold)
vol g ≠ 0

hypotheses.paper: « choose v supported in the interior with ∫_Σ v ≠ 0 » (l.401)
hypotheses.note: InteriorBump: v of finite energy, tr v = 0 a.e. on every B_j, ∫ val v ≠ 0; used for cap* < ∞ only

hypotheses.paper: the direct method (l.402–404): bounded sets weakly compact, ℓ weakly continuous by compactness of the trace
hypotheses.note: DirectMethod: a finite-energy sequence bounded in W^{1,2} with energies → e has a subsequence converging in L²(Σ) and in every L²(B_j) to some v ∈ D of energy ≤ e; used for the attainment only. A W^{1,2} reading: the C¹ reading of OQ-93 (b) is not weakly closed
GradMeasurable, for the Euler–Lagrange system only (the polarisation of the energy needs integrable densities)
eq:capineq holds for every u ∈ D (capineq); in multiplied form √cap*·ℓ(u) ≤ ‖∇u‖ for every u of finite energy with no hypothesis at all (sqrt_capStar_mul_ell_le)

labels.open_part: The strong form of the Euler–Lagrange system (Δv = μ/(2V) in Σ, ∂_ν v = −μ w_j/(2|B_j|) on B_j) is not stated: the model has no Laplacian and no normal derivative; its weak form ∫⟨∇v,∇φ⟩ = (μ/2)ℓ(φ) for every φ of finite energy, and the pairing ‖∇v‖² = (μ/2)ℓ(v) = μ/2, are proved (euler_lagrange). The carried Props MeanPoincare, TraceBound, InteriorBump, DirectMethod, GradMeasurable are not discharged on a manifold reading here; all five hold on the two-point toy model (toy_lem_capstar_hyps), where cap* = 8 (toy_capStar)
findings: l.386–387 with l.249: the paper writes the homogenised operator as −Δ + V (l.249), i.e. Δ = div∇. With that Δ and the outward normal the printed system Δv = μ/(2V), ∂_ν v = −μw_j/(2|B_j|) is inconsistent: the divergence theorem gives ∫_Σ Δv = μ/2 while ∫_{∂Σ} ∂_ν v = −(μ/2)Σ_j w_j = −μ/2, forcing μ = 0, but μ = 2cap* > 0. The Euler–Lagrange system of eq:capstar is −Δv = μ/(2V), ∂_ν v = −μw_j/(2|B_j|) (ν outward), i.e. the printed one with Δ = −div∇. Its weak form ∫⟨∇v,∇φ⟩ = (μ/2)ℓ(φ) is what Yamabe.MeasuredModel.euler_lagrange proves; the sign computation itself is argued, not formalized (the model has no Laplacian)

l.399–400: the paper's explicit lower bound cap* ≥ [‖ℓ‖(1+λ_1^{-1/2})]^{-2} is proved as stated (capStar_ge, with Λ = ‖ℓ‖ and K = λ_1⁻¹); the bound only needs |ℓ(v)| ≤ L‖∇v‖ (capStar_ge_of_abs_ell_le)

l.379: positivity of cap* needs neither the finiteness nor the attainment; and if cap* = ∞ then ℓ vanishes on every function of finite energy (ell_eq_zero_of_capStar_eq_top), so eq:capineq holds with any convention for 1/√∞
questions: The sign convention of Δ at l.386 (see findings). Reading taken: Δ = −div∇ (the nonnegative Laplacian) and ν the outward normal, the only convention under which the printed system is the Euler–Lagrange system; formalized in weak form only

λ_1 is « the first non-zero Neumann eigenvalue, equivalently the best constant in the Poincaré inequality » (l.319–321). Reading taken here: the Poincaré inequality with some finite constant K (MeanPoincare), which is all the proof of positivity uses; the eigenvalue reading is not formalized (T-perf-star3 defines λ_1 as a best constant, Yamabe.MeasuredModel.lambda1)

labels.label: lem:capacitary

hypotheses.paper: the setting of § 2–4 (compact, connected, non-empty Lipschitz boundary), through cap* > 0
hypotheses.note: the same carried Props as lem_capstar's positivity: MeanPoincare, TraceBound, ∃ j, bvol g j ≠ 0, vol g ≠ 0, finite measures
not used: lem_capacitary holds for every u ∈ D

findings: l.458–460 and l.502–509: lem:capacitary and lem:holder hold for every u, with no sign condition; applied to u and −u they give eq:linear with |ū| (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.eq_linear: V^{1/p*}|ū| ≤ C_1 X + C_2 Y for every u ∈ D). This confirms the planner's [r] for T-perf-main (a): the u ↦ |u| reduction is not needed for eq:linear; whether it is needed at the squaring step of thm:main depends only on whether eq:star is available for signed u (T-perf-star3's StarIneqSigned)

labels.label: lem:holder

hypotheses.note: IsFiniteMeasure (bvol g j)

hypotheses.paper: the trace of u ∈ W^{1,2} lies in L^{p♯}(B_j) (l.134)
hypotheses.note: per u: ∀ j, MemLp (tr u) p♯ (bvol g j); without it the junk value normSq = 0 would make the inequality false
not used; the inequality holds in absolute value (abs_bdryAvg_le)

hypotheses.paper: every |B_j| > 0 and n ≥ 1 (implicit: |B_j|^{-2/p♯}, a minimiser on the simplex)
hypotheses.note: ∀ j, bvol g j ≠ 0 and 0 < n, for the minimisation part only; n ≥ 1 is standing by DEC-186
holderObj_eq: Σ w_j²|B_j|^{-2/p♯} = 1/S + Σ (w_j − w*_j)²|B_j|^{-2/p♯} on the whole hyperplane Σ w_j = 1, so w* is the unique minimiser there too; lem_holder states the simplex form

findings: l.497–500 (commentary after lem:holder): « the naive uniform choice loses a factor n^{1/(N−1)} over n equal components ». For n components of equal area the optimal weights are themselves uniform, w_j = 1/n (capWeight_of_equal), so no choice of weights loses anything there; the factor is S/|∂Σ|^{2/p♯} = n^{1/(N−1)} (bdryS_of_equal), the loss of one Hölder over all of ∂Σ instead of one per component, as the first half of the sentence (« rather than (Σ_j|B_j|)^{2/p♯} ») says

kb_proposals: pattern: an infimum that the paper proves finite (cap*) is best defined in ℝ≥0∞ over the honest energy ∫⁻ ofReal |∇v|² (MeasuredModel.energy), not over the real dirichlet: inf ∅ = ∞ and infinite-energy functions contribute ∞, so « 0 < cap* < ∞ » is a real statement; take .toReal only where it is finite (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.capStar)

pattern: eq:capineq-type inequalities from an infimum hold with no hypothesis in multiplied form (√cap*·ℓ(u) ≤ ‖∇u‖ for finite-energy u, sqrt_capStar_mul_ell_le); the divided form needs 0 < cap* < ∞; infinite-energy u are handled by the bound |ℓ| ≤ L√dirichlet, whose junk 0 forces ℓ(u) = 0
